A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same research framework and experimental study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 Section 6 and Appendix L report original Bellman–Ford experiments, including size generalization, expressivity comparisons, regularization ablations, and training dynamics.

after.justification: v2 Section 5 and Appendix N retain those experiments and add results for deeper networks, repeated model application, and Cora/Citeseer graphs.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix N introduces a limited inference extension: applying the trained two-layer MPNN twice to predict four Bellman–Ford steps. The underlying message-passing functions, weighted regularization objective, and training-set construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds Cora and Citeseer as real-world graph evaluations and extends the tested Bellman–Ford prediction horizon to four steps. The original synthetic graph families and two-/three-step tasks remain covered.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain standard 1-WL versus individualized 1-iWL MPNNs and the proposed regularizer versus ordinary ℓ1 and ℓ2 regularization. The added experiments examine configurations and repeated use of the existing MPNN.

E3.justification: v2 Table 7 adds three-layer training for three Bellman–Ford steps and two successive applications of a two-layer model for four steps, evaluated on 64-node General and ER graphs. Existing protocols, metrics, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: The new depth-matched experiment tests whether three layers address the previously observed failure of two layers on three steps. A repeated-application experiment additionally tests extending the learned computation. The original failure case, regularization ablations, and weight analyses remain.

E5.justification: The original three-seed averaging statements, ± reporting, and single-seed smoothed training curves are retained. New tables use the existing ± format without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure or an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: Original tabulated results are unchanged, including v1 Tables 7–8 retained as v2 Tables 9–10. New Table 7 reports General/ER scores of 0.0075/0.0155 for three-layer prediction and 0.0040/0.0051 for repeated application. New Table 8 reports 0.0083/0.0080 on Cora/Citeseer. These additions use different conditions from the original results.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2.2.1 removes v1's assertion that graph diameter bounds the required Bellman–Ford iterations and limits the argument to learning K iterations. Appendix B.4 also adds a formal source-to-target shortest-path definition. The principal theorem statements, bounds, and appendix proofs otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same finite-data learnability framework, expressivity limitations, and Bellman–Ford regularization contribution. Explicitly describing the guarantees as worst-case restates the uniform guarantees already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies the distinction between marked-source Bellman–Ford learning and impossibility results without individualization. Its limitations section newly explains that the general cover-based guarantee is nonconstructive and potentially computationally expensive, while the Bellman–Ford training set is explicit.

D1.justification: The existing implementation descriptions, dataset generators, hyperparameter grid, hardware, runtime/memory table, and code-access URL are retained. The new experiments add evaluation configurations but little additional implementation or preprocessing documentation.

R1.justification: The introduction more explicitly acknowledges prior sample-complexity and PAC-style guarantees and distinguishes the paper's worst-case extrapolation setting. Related work adds Požgaj et al. (2025) on knapsack reasoning, while the Weisfeiler (1976) reference is removed. Most cited research and positioning remain.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: detailed related work moves to Appendix A, extensive background moves to Appendix B, and the main text is condensed. It adds a main-text proof sketch, motivation and scope explanations, acknowledgements, and an impact statement, while removing the contents listing.

P2.justification: The single-column report becomes a two-column main paper with extensively reformatted typography, captions, tables, and figure placement. Two appendix tables are added; existing figures are retained and resized or repositioned, and the former Tables 7–8 become Tables 9–10.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision by removing the diameter-based Bellman–Ford assertion and explaining source marking and the limits of constructing training covers. Added depth and repeated-application tests complement the retained failure case, while real-world graphs broaden empirical support. The central proofs and original results remain stable, and the added experiments are documented briefly, making the overall gain useful but limited.
